pharm: Selectively blocks alpha-1A/alpha-1D adrenoceptors in the prostate, bladder neck, and prostatic urethra, relaxing smooth muscle and improving urine flow in BPH.
quick: 0.4 mg once daily; may increase to 0.8 mg
Take 30 minutes after the same meal each day
Not indicated in women; limited data
No initial adjustment in mild-moderate impairment
Caution; not studied in severe impairment
Blood pressure, orthostatic symptoms, IFIS at cataract surgery
summary: Tamsulosin is a uroselective alpha-1 adrenergic blocker used to relieve the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate and bladder neck to improve urinary flow. It is taken once daily about half an hour after the same meal. Key cautions include orthostatic hypotension, first-dose syncope, priapism, and intraoperative floppy iris syndrome during cataract surgery. It is not indicated for hypertension.
indications: Treatment of the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)

dosage.t: Once daily, ~30 min after the same meal

dosage.d: Increase to 0.8 mg once daily after 2-4 weeks
dosage.n: For those who fail to respond to 0.4 mg
If discontinued/interrupted for several days, re-initiate at 0.4 mg

dosage.d: Avoid 0.4 mg with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole)
dosage.n: Use caution with CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitor combinations

admin: Swallow capsule whole; do not crush, chew, or open
Take approximately 30 minutes after the same meal each day
Take the first dose at bedtime to reduce first-dose orthostatic hypotension
Re-initiate at 0.4 mg if therapy is interrupted for several days
moa: Tamsulosin selectively antagonizes alpha-1A (and alpha-1D) adrenergic receptors that predominate in the prostate, prostatic capsule, prostatic urethra, and bladder neck. This relaxes the smooth muscle in these tissues, decreasing urethral resistance and improving urinary flow and BPH symptoms. Its relative uroselectivity produces less effect on vascular smooth muscle and blood pressure than non-selective alpha-blockers.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to tamsulosin or any formulation component (including angioedema)
relative: Planned cataract or glaucoma surgery (intraoperative floppy iris syndrome)

preg: Tamsulosin is not indicated for use in women; human pregnancy data are lacking.
lact: Tamsulosin is not indicated for use in women; use during lactation is not applicable.
renal: No initial dosage adjustment is needed in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment; tamsulosin has not been adequately studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <10 mL/min) and should be used with caution.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment; tamsulosin has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment and should be used with caution.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir) - increase tamsulosin exposure; avoid 0.4 mg dose
PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - additive hypotension
Other alpha-blockers - not recommended in combination (additive hypotension)
moderate: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., paroxetine) - increase exposure
interactions.food: Take about 30 minutes after the same meal each day; fasting increases absorption and exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate dizziness and orthostatic hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference established.

monitoring: Blood pressure and orthostatic symptoms (especially first dose)
Ophthalmic surgical history before cataract surgery
counsel: Take the same time each day, about half an hour after the same meal
Swallow whole; do not crush, chew, or open the capsule
Rise slowly from sitting or lying; first dose may cause dizziness or fainting
Tell your eye surgeon you take this drug before any cataract surgery
Seek urgent care for a painful erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
pk: 4-5 hours fed; 6-7 hours after repeated dosing
9-13 hours (healthy); up to ~15 hours in target population
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Uroselective: less effect on blood pressure than non-selective alpha-blockers but orthostasis still occurs
Strongly associated with intraoperative floppy iris syndrome - always disclose before cataract surgery
Retrograde/abnormal ejaculation is a common, benign but bothersome effect
Re-titrate from 0.4 mg if therapy is interrupted for several days
Not an antihypertensive; do not use to treat high blood pressure
missed: Take the missed dose with the next meal; if it is close to the next scheduled dose, skip it and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause severe hypotension. Treat by placing the patient supine to restore blood pressure and normalize heart rate; use intravenous fluids and, if needed, vasopressors. Dialysis is unlikely to help given high protein binding. Monitor renal function and support as needed.
